text_span: This study explores the integration of quantum computing principles into financial regime detection through a hybrid quantum–classical support vector machine (SVM) framework.
rationale: States the paper’s central research objective and model framing.

text_span: hybrid models achieve accuracy levels close to classical models (≈81%) while enhancing recall balance across extreme market regimes.
rationale: Summarizes the main performance finding for hybrid models.

text_span: classical and quantum components agree on approximately 62% of predictions
rationale: Reports the internal agreement statistic used to assess complementarity.

text_span: hybrid architectures maintain near-linear training costs, avoiding the exponential time burden observed in fully quantum models.
rationale: States the computational efficiency claim for the hybrid design.

text_span: quantum-enhanced models offer a fundamentally richer representational capacity, capable to embed financial data into Hilbert spaces that are exponentially large
rationale: Frames the theoretical motivation for quantum feature spaces.

text_span: The quantum component operates as a complementary subsystem, instead of replacing conventional models.
rationale: Defines the intended role of the quantum component in the study.

text_span: Comparative analyses examine accuracy, recall, F1 symmetry, and training-time efficiency across Classical SVM, Quantum SVM, and Hybrid (80–20 / 60-–40) configurations.
rationale: Describes the comparative evaluation design and metrics.

text_span: The experimental dataset integrates multiple macro–financial dimensions of the U.S. market between February 2006 and October 2025.
rationale: Specifies the dataset scope and time span.

text_span: Equities (SPY) for aggregate risk appetite.
rationale: Identifies one of the engineered data domains; similar domains are listed in the same paragraph.

text_span: A standardized transformation pipeline was applied to every time series to ensure cross–domain comparability.
rationale: States the preprocessing strategy applied across all series.

text_span: Return Generation: both arithmetic and logarithmic returns were computed
rationale: Captures a key feature-engineering decision.

text_span: all series were winsorized at the 1st and 99th percentiles to reduce the influence of extreme shocks
rationale: Documents a data-cleaning and normalization choice.

text_span: three widely used classical classification algorithms were implemented: Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and a Support Vector Machine with Radial Basis Function kernel (SVM–RBF).
rationale: Identifies the classical baseline models used for comparison.

text_span: To prevent information leakage and mimic real–world forecasting conditions, a chronological split was used rather than random sampling
rationale: Explains the temporal validation design.

text_span: All scores were computed using macro–averaging to account for the three-class structure
rationale: Specifies the metric aggregation approach.

text_span: a Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC) was developed using Qiskit Machine Learning
rationale: Introduces the quantum model implementation platform.

text_span: The implementation employed the Fidelity Statevector Kernel, a noiseless simulation of quantum state overlaps
rationale: Defines the quantum kernel used in the QSVC.

code_label: PCA dimensionality reduction to six components
text_span: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was employed to project the standardized features into six orthogonal principal components
rationale: States the dimensionality reduction step before quantum encoding.

text_span: the Synthetic Minority Over–sampling Technique (SMOTE) was applied with an oversampling ratio of 0.6
rationale: Documents the class-balancing procedure.

text_span: Each standardized feature vector x∈ℝ6 was encoded into a six–qubit quantum state using the ZZFeatureMap
rationale: Specifies the quantum feature map architecture.

text_span: The chosen configuration utilized three repetitions (r=3) of the feature map with full entanglement
rationale: Captures the circuit depth and entanglement choice.

text_span: constructing the full kernel matrix requires evaluating all pairwise fidelities among n samples, leading to quadratic time complexity O(n2)
rationale: States the computational scaling of the quantum kernel.

text_span: On average, the end–to–end training phase required roughly one hour
rationale: Reports the observed training time for the QSVC pipeline.

text_span: the model achieved a training accuracy of 85.3% and a test accuracy of 66.0%, corresponding to an overfitting gap of approximately 19 percentage points.
rationale: Reports the main quantum model performance and generalization gap.

text_span: a Hybrid Quantum–Classical Support Vector Machine (Hybrid QSVM) was implemented.
rationale: Introduces the hybrid architecture evaluated in the paper.

text_span: These included configurations such as 60–40 and 70–30 weighting schemes that assign greater influence on the classical SVM
rationale: Describes the ensemble weighting variants.

text_span: the quantum SVM was trained on a representative subset of approximately 2,000 samples, whereas the classical SVM utilized the full balanced set of roughly 4,600 samples.
rationale: Documents the differing sample sizes used in the hybrid setup.

text_span: hybrid predictions were generated through deterministic weighted voting
rationale: Specifies the ensemble decision rule.

text_span: XGBoost achieved the best overall performance, with an accuracy of approximately 71.8% and an F1–score of 0.70.
rationale: Reports the top classical baseline result.

text_span: all three algorithms completed training in under one minute on standard CPU hardware
rationale: Summarizes the classical models’ computational efficiency.

text_span: scaling the training set from 2,000 to 3,500 samples produced only marginal improvement in minority–class F1
rationale: Indicates limited gains from increasing quantum training data.

text_span: The minority (Bullish) regime achieved an F1–score of 0.20
rationale: Reports the quantum model’s minority-class performance.

text_span: Hybrid configurations substantially improve generalization compared with the standalone Quantum SVM.
rationale: States the main hybrid improvement over the quantum-only model.

text_span: The Classical SVM retains the highest test accuracy at 80.43%, while Hybrid (50–50) and (60–40) ensembles achieve 75.9% and 75.4%, respectively
rationale: Provides the key hybrid-vs-classical accuracy comparison.

text_span: improving minority–class detection (Regime +1 F1 ≈0.53–0.56), a notable gain over the quantum baseline (0.19).
rationale: Reports the hybrid gain in minority-class F1.

text_span: The Classical and Quantum components agree on approximately 62% of all predictions
rationale: Reports the agreement statistic used to assess complementarity.

text_span: Hybrid ensembles achieve more than 90% of classical accuracy at a fraction of the quantum computational cost.
rationale: Summarizes the efficiency-performance trade-off for hybrids.

text_span: hybridization represents a pragmatic intermediate frontier between conventional and quantum machine learning
rationale: States the paper’s interpretive conclusion about hybridization.

text_span: All quantum components in this study were executed on simulated backends rather than physical quantum processors.
rationale: Explicitly states a key limitation of the study.

text_span: Future implementations should explore adaptive weighting between classical and quantum components.
rationale: Identifies a concrete future research direction.
